declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Hargrove Lane LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, submits this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The settlement resulted from an exchange of proposals addressing both class relief and attorneys’ fees. Fees were discussed beginning with the opening proposal, not deferred until after agreement on class relief. Counsel initially proposed a $32 million class fund and $5 million in fees and expenses; Brightline countered with $24 million and $4 million, respectively. Counsel next proposed $29 million and $4.5 million, and Brightline countered with $26 million and $4 million. Counsel then proposed $28 million for the class and accepted the proposed $4 million fee amount while class relief remained unresolved. Brightline proposed a $27 million class fund and $4 million in fees and expenses, which counsel accepted in the fourth round.

The binding settlement provides automatic distribution using Brightline’s existing records, without requiring class members to submit claims. The $4 million fee-and-expense request is subject to court approval; Brightline retains its right to oppose it. Any amount not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. The agreed $31 million aggregate includes notice, administration, distribution, and incremental implementation cash expenses. Accordingly, the $27 million class fund should not be represented as the net amount members will receive. The parties agreed to obtain competitive administrator quotes, establish a documented, court-reviewable implementation budget and cap before submission, and disclose estimated net member payments. Unused administrative reserves will remain for class members. The negotiation record does not establish that those estimates and budget documents have yet been completed.

Counsel believes the settlement is fair to the class and warrants preliminary approval, subject to the Court’s review of the implementation budget, proposed allocation and notice, and other required approval materials. The $27 million gross class fund represents approximately 42% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges. It provides substantial recovery without the unresolved risks of class certification and trial or the anticipated two-to-three-year delay before trial. Automatic distribution avoids a claims-filing barrier where Brightline can identify every class member and the card charged. Independent fee review, the absence of clear sailing, and allocation of unawarded fees to the class are additional protections. Counsel nevertheless acknowledges that fees and class relief were negotiated together; counsel does not ask the Court to treat the negotiations as sequential or to infer fairness from a separation that did not occur. Final approval and the fee award remain subject to independent judicial scrutiny under Rule 23(e) and the applicable fee standards.
